columns.description: Cedar device-observation key. The prefix names the upstream evidence: CAP=gaming_capacity_official, WI=Wisconsin LFB via state_gaming_observations, WAA=wa_machine_allocations, CST=compact_structured_terms, OK=Oklahoma OMES (new extraction), AZR=Arizona ADG FY2025 annual report (new extraction).
columns.name: observation_id

columns.description: Existing Cedar property ID (CCP-/VP-/TPL-). BLANK where the observation is about a tribe or a whole state rather than a property. No property ID is created by this build; a regulator or manufacturer using a different property name is an ALIAS.
columns.name: facility_id

columns.description: Cedar spine entity ID. BLANK on statewide rows by design.
columns.name: tribe_id

columns.description: The date the source's figure is AS OF. Oklahoma rows use the 30 June state fiscal year end.
columns.name: observation_date

columns.description: SHIPMENT_IN | SHIPMENT_OUT | DEVICE_ADDITION | DEVICE_REMOVAL | REGULATORY_INVENTORY | MANUFACTURER_PLACEMENT | FLOOR_COUNT | FLEET_REPLACEMENT | AUTHORIZED_MAXIMUM. REGULATORY_INVENTORY = a regulator's count of devices in place. FLOOR_COUNT = the operator's own signed statement of its floor. AUTHORIZED_MAXIMUM = a ceiling or entitlement and NEVER an operating count.
columns.name: observation_type

columns.description: Who built the devices. Populated only where a source names the manufacturer for a specific dated placement. No free source does so, so this column is empty; the emptiness is the finding.
columns.name: manufacturer

columns.description: Cabinet or platform name. Empty for the same reason as manufacturer.
columns.name: platform_or_cabinet

columns.description: Game title. Empty for the same reason as manufacturer.
columns.name: game_theme

columns.description: Class II / Class III / Class III (DCETG) / Class III (Tribal Lottery System player terminal), AS STATED BY THE SOURCE ON THIS DATE. Blank means the source did not say, never 'unknown class'. THIS IS AN OBSERVATION FIELD, NOT A PROPERTY ATTRIBUTE: a floor can be converted between classes with no federal record, so class is a necessary but not sufficient condition and must always be read with its date.
examples: Class III (Tribal Lottery System player terminal)
columns.name: device_class

columns.description: Number of devices. Blank where the source asserts a right or a category without a number - a blank quantity is silence, not zero.
columns.name: quantity

columns.description: Shipping party on a device movement. Empty: no free source publishes shipment-level detail.
columns.name: shipment_origin

columns.description: Receiving party on a device movement. Empty for the same reason.
columns.name: shipment_destination

columns.description: cedar_domain.MeasurementType. may_promote() is asserted per row: AUTHORIZED_MAXIMUM, PROJECTED, ENVIRONMENTAL_REVIEW_COUNT and DERIVED_BOUND can never be presented as an active floor count.
columns.name: measurement_type

columns.description: The publisher's URL. Present on every row without exception.
columns.name: source_url

columns.description: Verbatim supporting text. Present on every row without exception; a row missing it is refused to the review queue.
examples: Casino "Mohegan Sun", Date "12/31/2025", Fiscal Year "2025/2026", "Weighted Aver

columns.name: source_quote

columns.description: When the underlying document was retrieved.
columns.name: fetched_date

columns.description: cedar_domain.Tier. A publishes; B is internal only. B here means the observation is real but its property or tribe is not resolved.
columns.name: tier

columns.description: What KIND of evidence this is, in words, not a number.
columns.name: confidence

columns.description: Build date of this row.
columns.name: built_date

columns.description: The Native entity this row ultimately belongs to, reached through the FACILITY, not by matching this row's own text. A casino is a hub: the facility carries the link to the entity and every source hanging off it inherits that link. Equal to gaming_facilities.tribe_id for the facility named in facility_id.
columns.name: entity_id

columns.description: Whether the link is to a PROPERTY (`facility`) or only to the operating entity (`tribe`). A tribe-level row is a fact about the entity and is NOT attributable to any one of its properties - an online sportsbook is not a building and a compact authorises a tribe.
columns.name: entity_level

columns.description: Confidence tier of the ENTITY LINK, INHERITED verbatim from the facility row that carries it. It is never assigned by the table that holds it. An exact join on facility_id is exact; that says nothing about whether the facility itself was correctly keyed, and treating an exact key as strong evidence is the error that attributed a Wisconsin United Way to a California tribe at tier A.
columns.name: entity_tier

columns.description: Where entity_tier came from, in words, so a reader can see that it was inherited rather than assigned. Blank tier plus a stated basis means no tier could be inherited and none was invented.
examples: mirrored from this row's own tier
columns.name: entity_tier_basis

columns.description: Which rung produced the link. `facility_id_exact` - the row names a facility that exists in the hub and carries an entity. `multi_property_host_unanimous_tribe` - a website host serving several properties that all belong to one tribe; linked at tribe level only, at the WEAKEST tier in the group. `row_tribe_id_mirror` - the row is tribe-level by design and this mirrors a link an earlier build made; it creates no new link. `ruled_nigc_name_exact` - an exact join into gaming_nigc_roster_link, a ruled table. `not_tribe_attributable_by_source` - the source states this licensee is not a Native entity; a correct answer, not a gap. NO RUNG USES A COORDINATE: proximity is weaker evidence than a name, and running it first let `Sportman's Bar` claim `4 Bears Casino & Lodge`.
columns.name: entity_link_rung

columns.description: Date this row's entity link was written.
columns.name: entity_link_date
